submission.natural_language_explanation: L1/H6 attends from each token to one salient earlier token (usually 1-7 back) and copies it. It is strong (above about 0.55 of max) when that anchor is (a) a demonstrative 'that' used as determiner or pronoun subject (peak on the next token: 'that amount/point/day/song', "that's", 'that is'), (b) a subject 'it' followed by 'is'/'s' (peak on 'is' and the next adjective: 'it is possible/clear/impossible'), (c) sports-statistics vocabulary ('scored', 'batting', 'yards', 'assists', 'team won', 'League', 'World Cup'; peaks on the stat nouns, numbers and 'per'/'and' after them), or (d) an opening '$' of inline math or a 'k*' coefficient in algebra (peak on the closing '$' or the variable). Plain prose is NOT silent: most ordinary determiner/preposition+noun sentences cross the 0.25 line weakly (0.25-0.45 of max) on their subject noun or main verb, so predict them active-weak. Predict inactive (below the line) only for comma lists of numbers, weekdays or names, strings of one-word sentences ('Yes. No. Maybe.'), brace-heavy code, and complementizer or relative 'that' with no other anchor ('The motion that failed was reintroduced later.').
